He currently operates Wes Johnson Basketball, a private basketball training business based in [[New Orleans]], [[Louisiana]], offering coaching for high school, college, and competitive athletes.{{Cite web|title=Wes Johnson Basketball|url=https://www.wesjbasketball.com|access-date=May 5, 2026|website=wesjbasketball.com}} He previously served as a player development assistant for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).{{Cite web|title=The Clippers promote Shaun Fein, add Wesley Johnson and Cookie Belcher to their coaching staff|url=https://www.clipsnation.com/2021/9/26/22692179/la-clippers-news-2021-22-coaching-staff-shaun-fein-player-development-wesley-johnson-cookie-belcher|access-date=November 27, 2021|website=SBNation|date=26 September 2021 }} He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]] and [[Syracuse Orange basketball|Syracuse Orange]]. He was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] with the fourth overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?columnist=oneil_dana&id=4765334 |title=Dana O'Neil: Big East early season review – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=December 23, 2009 |access-date=March 22, 2010}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=4818431 |title=Jay Bilas' Midseason All-American team – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=January 12, 2010 |access-date=March 22, 2010}} ==Early life== In high school, he averaged 15.2 points, 9.7 rebounds and 4.3 blocks as a senior at [[Corsicana High School]]. He was a first-team all-district pick in 2004 and 2005.{{cite web|url=http://www.cyclones.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=46664&SPID=4252&DB_OEM_ID=10700&ATCLID=329810&Q_SEASON=2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100811015122/http://www.cyclones.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=46664&SPID=4252&DB_OEM_ID=10700&ATCLID=329810&Q_SEASON=2007 |title=Wesley Johnson – Iowa State University Athletics|publisher=www.CYCLONES.com |access-date=March 22, 2010 |archive-date=August 11, 2010 |url-status=dead}} He also played for the Dallas Mustangs [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] team. ==College career== [[File:Wesley Johnson Providence College Syracuse (cropped).jpg|upright=0.7|thumb|left|Johnson with Syracuse in 2010]] As a freshman at [[Iowa State University|Iowa State]], Johnson was named to the Big 12 all-Rookie team and earned honorable mention freshman All-America honors after averaging 12.3 points and 7.9 rebounds, starting 30 of 31 games. Johnson's highlights from his freshman year included 14 points and 13 rebounds in win against Missouri, including the game-winner on a tip-in with 1.6 seconds left. He also scored 17 points at No. 10 [[Texas A&M Aggies|Texas A&M]]. Johnson missed five games and played with an injured ankle throughout the majority of the season. He still was named an honorable mention all-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] selection after averaging 12.4 points and 4.0 rebounds per game. Johnson scored 20 points behind a 5-of-11 effort from 3-point range against eventual NCAA Champion [[Kansas Jayhawks|Kansas]]. Johnson made the decision to transfer following the 2008 season, and selected [[Syracuse Orange|Syracuse]]. Per NCAA transfer rules, he had to sit out the 2008–09 season, leaving him with two years of college eligibility.{{cite web |url=http://media.www.dailyorange.com/media/storage/paper522/news/2008/05/08/Sports/Mbb-Syracuse.Lands.Iowa.State.Tranfer.Johnson-3385520.shtml |title=Daily Orange – MBB | Syracuse lands Iowa State transfer Johnson |publisher=Media.www.dailyorange.com |access-date=March 22, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090211025911/http://media.www.dailyorange.com/media/storage/paper522/news/2008/05/08/Sports/Mbb-Syracuse.Lands.Iowa.State.Tranfer.Johnson-3385520.shtml |archive-date=February 11, 2009 |url-status=dead }} Johnson became a starter for the Orange in his first year with the team. In November 2009 he was named MVP of the 2K Coaches Classic after scoring 25 points in a Syracuse victory over the No. 6 [[North Carolina Tar Heels|North Carolina]].{{cite Inks Monroe|access-date=May 13, 2010|date=May 11, 2010|publisher=[[Street & Smith]]|work=[[SportsBusiness Daily]]|author=Mullen, Liz}} ==Professional career== === Minnesota Timberwolves (2010–2012) === [[File:Wesley Johnson-MN v DET.jpg|thumb|Johnson with the Timberwolves in January 2012]] Johnson was drafted by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] with the 4th pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. On March 18, 2011, Johnson scored a career-high 29 points on 11-for-21 shooting in a loss against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. === Phoenix Suns (2012–2013) === On July 27, 2012, Johnson was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in a three-team deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/suns-acquire-johnson-and-pick-trade-lopez-and-warrick|title=Suns Acquire Johnson and Pick, Trade Lopez and Warrick|work=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2012|access-date=July 29, 2012}} In his first game with the Suns, Johnson scored a three-pointer in a close victory against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. Johnson would not gain significant playing time with the Suns until [[Lindsey Hunter]] took over as head coach for the team. On February 26, 2013, Johnson recorded 14 points, along with 9 rebounds, 3 assists, and 2 steals in an 84–83 victory against his former team, the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. A day later, Johnson made a game-tying three-pointer from a long pass by [[Jermaine O'Neal]] that helped the Suns win 105–101 in overtime against the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. On March 1, 2013, Johnson scored a season high 15 points and added six rebounds and two steals in a 92–87 victory against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400278594|title=Twins Marcus and Markieff Morris help Suns win third straight game|work=ESPN|date=March 1, 2013|access-date=February 18, 2023|agency=Associated Press|location=Phoenix}} === Los Angeles Lakers (2013–2015) === On July 15, 2013, Johnson signed a one-year deal with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Wesley Johnson|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/130715wesleyjohnson|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2013|access-date=July 27, 2014}} In his first season with the Lakers, Johnson averaged career highs in points, rebounds, steals and blocks. He was one of only eight players in the league to average at least 1 block and 1 steal per game, and the only perimeter player to do so. He had four games where he scored 20 or more points, the most since his rookie season. On November 29, 2013, Johnson recorded 27 points, along with 6 rebounds and 3 blocks, in a 106–102 victory against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. He tallied four [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double-doubles]] over the course of the season, a career high. On July 28, 2014, Johnson re-signed with the Lakers on a one-year deal.{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Wesley Johnson|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140728wesleyJohnson|work=NBA.com|date=July 28, 2014|access-date=July 28, 2014}} === Los Angeles Clippers (2015–2018) === On July 9, 2015, Johnson signed a one-year deal with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite news|title=CLIPPERS RE-SIGN JORDAN AND SIGN JOHNSON|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/free-agency-2015|access-date=July 9, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2015}} He made his debut for the Clippers in the team's season opener against the Sacramento Kings on October 28, recording 3 points and 1 steal in a 111–104 win.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/LACSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Griffin leads Clippers past Kings 111–104 in opener|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015}} On July 8, 2016, Johnson re-signed with the Clippers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-re-sign-free-agents-crawford-johnson-mbah-moute-and-rivers|title=Press Release: Clippers Re-sign Free Agents Crawford, Johnson, Mbah A Moute And Rivers|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=July 8, 2016}} === New Orleans Pelicans (2018–2019) === On October 15, 2018, Johnson was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for [[Alexis Ajinça]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-wesley-johnson|title=Pelicans acquire Wesley Johnson|work=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2018|access-date=October 15, 2018}} ===Washington Wizards (2019)=== On February 7, 2019, Johnson was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Markieff Morris]] and a 2023 second-round pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-acquire-johnson-pelicans|title=Wizards acquire Johnson from Pelicans|work=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2019|access-date=February 7, 2019}} On April 5, 2019, Johnson was waived by the Wizards.{{cite web|title=Wizards waive Wesley Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-waive-wesley-johnson|date=April 5, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 5, 2019}} === Panathinaikos (2019–2020) === On July 22, 2019, Johnson signed a one-year deal with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=Panathinaikos lands veteran forward Johnson|url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9tgnq3x8875ni6b5/panathinaikos-lands-veteran-forward-johnson | date=July 22, 2019|website=EuroLeague.net|access-date=July 22, 2019}} In his first career game with Panathinaikos, Johnson scored 7 points in 19 minutes of playing time against AEK Athens.{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Greece/2019/0928_92_275.asp|title=Panathinaikos 89 - AEK Athens 65|publisher=EuroBasket|date=September 28, 2019|access-date=June 29, 2020}} ==Career
